also: I really like it a lot

terms.gloss: I like it, it pleases me
terms.grammar: impersonal: the thing liked is the subject, the person in the dative
terms.comment: English “I like this” turns round: hoc mihi placet, “this pleases me”. “Do you like it?”: placetne tibi?.

terms.grammar: impersonal, with the person in the accusative and an infinitive
evidence: Hor. S. 2.6.32: hoc juvat et mellī est
terms.comment: For liking to do something: mē juvat hoc facere, I like doing this (see enjoy).

phrases.latin: ecquid placeant, mē rogās? immō herclē vērō perplacent
phrases.english: you ask whether I like them? why, I like them very much indeed
Heavens, yes. I really like it a lot.

phrases.latin: Nempe audīre clāmōrēs fautōrum mihi placet.
phrases.english: Naturally, I like to hear the cheers of the fans.

sources: Lewis & Short: placeo · Lewis & Short: juvo
